headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared data flows and broad egress create leakage and cascading-error exposure; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented between airbyte and cognee, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, cognee’s CLI/session-memory design and airbyte’s API-facing data integration role mean a manual or pipeline bridge could exist if operators connect outputs to inputs. Uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF an operator copies airbyte output into cognee prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared workspace or queue, untrusted content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of raw outputs into cognee prompts.
Add a review step before any airbyte-exported text is ingested by cognee.
Use a provenance tag on imported content.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while cognee touches personal, finance, and support data and can call external APIs via LLM_API_KEY/COGNEE_SERVICE_URL. Even without a documented shared filesystem, a default integration path could move sensitive data from one agent into the other’s outbound requests. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible and not blocked by default.
conditions: IF airbyte exports business data into cognee-managed context, that data can be re-sent over cognee API calls.
IF either agent is configured to process the other’s outputs as input, sensitive fields may traverse both systems.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a test dataset.
Remove secrets and personal data before transfer.
Turn off broad egress where possible.
Use separate service accounts and API keys.
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before any cross-agent handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: airbyte has broad network egress and API access, while cognee supports multiple instances and CLI-based operation with session memory. The profiles do not show shared write locks or a shared mutable resource, so a high-severity write collision is not proven. Still, overlapping operational control over data/workflow state makes conflict plausible in default multi-instance deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream dataset or workflow store, state conflicts can occur.
IF the orchestrator lacks locking, concurrent runs may overwrite each other’s outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories or databases.
Serialize runs through a simple operator checklist.
Use unique job IDs for each execution.
Check for existing locks before starting a run.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: airbyte is a data-integration system that can feed transformed data onward, and cognee is a memory/workflow system that can consume and act on stored context. If cognee treats airbyte outputs as authoritative, errors or malformed records can cascade into downstream decisions or workflows. The profiles do not prove automated action-taking, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF cognee ingests airbyte outputs without validation, upstream errors propagate downstream.
IF downstream workflows rely on cognee-stored facts, a bad record can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Add a validation step before ingestion.
Sample-check transformed records for correctness.
Mark imported fields as untrusted until reviewed.
Limit downstream actions to read-only mode during testing.
requires-engineering: implement schema and provenance verification.

E_compliance.rationale: airbyte touches business data, while cognee explicitly touches personal and finance data plus support history. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a direct regulatory breach is not proven. But the mixed data classes and broad egress create a realistic compliance mismatch risk if regulated data is routed through the wrong agent or retention policy.
conditions: IF personal or finance data is routed through airbyte or cognee without matching retention controls, policy mismatch occurs.
IF regulated data crosses a residency boundary not documented in either profile, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Keep regulated data out of cross-agent flows.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Review vendor terms before production use.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the pair.
